source_name: Temenos Success Stories / Customer Case Studies (incl. NLB success story)
why_relevant: Vendor-authored success story explicitly naming Nova Ljubljanska Banka (NLB), Slovenia's largest bank, as a Temenos core customer; contains deal scope detail (corporate core first, retail migration following N Banka migration) and vendor-claimed KPIs (time-to-market -50%, cost -25%). This is the single most detailed public record of the SI core-banking stack at the market leader.

source_name: Temenos Press Releases / Newsroom
why_relevant: First public record of new signings and go-lives; a Slovenian or SEE bank win is announced here before it appears anywhere else. Also a pointer to which local implementation partner ('local vendor') delivered the project.

source_name: Backbase Press & Media / Customer Stories
why_relevant: Leading digital-channel (engagement banking) vendor active in CEE/SEE. Its press and customer-story pages are the expected first record of any Slovenian digital-banking platform deal. No SI-named story found in this pass, so it is a monitoring target rather than a confirmed hit.

source_name: Infosys Finacle Client Stories
why_relevant: Global core-banking vendor with a structured, filterable client-story library; the canonical place a SI/SEE win would be documented. No Slovenian client surfaced in this pass — treat as monitoring target and as a benchmark for regional competitors.

source_name: Oracle Financial Services FLEXCUBE customer/case-study PDFs
why_relevant: Oracle publishes named bank case-study PDFs (e.g. Mashreq) under /a/ocom/docs/; if a Slovenian bank runs FLEXCUBE the reference would live here or in an IBS Intelligence co-branded PDF.

source_name: Mambu customer stories
why_relevant: Cloud core/lending vendor frequently used for greenfield and lending-only builds in CEE; its customer page is the natural first record of a Slovenian lender or bank subsidiary deal. URL inferred from vendor site structure and not confirmed in this pass — verify liveness downstream.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf banking case studies (global index)
why_relevant: Self-service/ATM-as-a-Service vendor that publishes named bank case studies across CEE (e.g. CSOB). Directly relevant to the self-service and cash-handling side of the SI market and a competitor-landscape signal for Printec-type integrators.

source_name: HRC d.o.o. — Hibis banking platform, Slovenian/Croatian bank client base
why_relevant: HRC describes itself as one of the largest suppliers of software for banks and savings banks in Slovenia and Croatia; its site names Slovenian clients (Addiko Bank, Delavska hranilnica, Gorenjska banka) and publishes Hibis implementation case examples. This is the highest-value *local* vendor-reference pointer for which SI institutions run which core stack — exactly the stack-mapping function the cell needs.

source_name: SETCCE — news / client references (digital signing & onboarding for SI banks)
why_relevant: Slovenian-language vendor news article explicitly enumerating bank clients (Sparkasse, Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica, NLB, Sberbank) for digital/e-signature solutions. A clean local-language example of the 'vendor announces the win' pattern and a pointer to which SI banks buy which digital-channel components.

source_name: Halcom — e-banking / payments vendor, bank reference lists
why_relevant: Halcom states it serves 50+ banks, 2 central banks and clearing houses, and introduced SEPA clearing at Banka Slovenije and Bankart. Its support pages enumerate which Slovenian banks support Hal E-Bank — an explicit bank-by-bank stack map for the corporate e-banking channel.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — payment systems and services (SI processing hub)
why_relevant: Bankart is the national card/payment processor for the Slovenian banking sector and an NLB Group company; its service and partner pages reveal which international vendors (e.g. Nets/Nexi for instant payments) sit behind the SI payments infrastructure, and which banks are participants. A pointer that enumerates both actors and vendor dependencies.

source_name: FinTech Futures — core banking technology desk (vendor-deal reporting)
why_relevant: Trade press that reliably reports vendor wins/go-lives that never reach a public portal, including Slovenia-specific items: NLB pioneering Temenos T24 R17, and Bankart+Nets delivering the SI instant-payments infrastructure. It also names the unnamed 'local vendor' layer that vendor marketing omits.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld customer databases (Temenos T24, Oracle FLEXCUBE, etc.)
why_relevant: Aggregator that enumerates named customers per banking product; useful for rapidly generating a candidate list of which SI/SEE institutions are attributed to which vendor, to be verified against primary vendor pages. Aggregated and partly paywalled, so treat as lead-generation not evidence.

source_name: FeaturedCustomers — vendor case-study/reference aggregator
why_relevant: Aggregates vendor-published case studies and references in one place per vendor, which shortens discovery of SI-named references across many banking vendors at once. Content is vendor-supplied marketing, so credibility inherits from the underlying vendor page.

source_name: Veeam customer stories — OTP banka (Slovenia)
why_relevant: Concrete confirmed example of the cell's core pattern outside core banking: an infrastructure vendor publishing a named Slovenian bank customer story (OTP banka, data protection for Microsoft 365). Establishes that infra/ISV customer-story pages are a productive vein for SI stack mapping and post-merger IT signals.

source_name: Humanfrog case studies — Sberbank banka (SI digital project)
why_relevant: Regional digital agency/integrator publishing a named case study for a bank operating in Slovenia (Sberbank, subsequently absorbed by NLB). Shows the second tier of the vendor landscape — digital agencies and integrators — which often documents projects that platform vendors never publish.

source_name: OTP banka Slovenija newsroom (Nova KBM + SKB IT merger reporting)
why_relevant: The bank's own Slovene-language releases on the largest bank merger in SI history describe an 18-month IT/system migration and the surviving digital-banking brands (Bank@Net, mBank@Net). Buyer-side corroboration that pins down which platform survived a merger — the counterpart evidence to any vendor case study.

source_name: NLB Group media centre / press releases
why_relevant: Buyer-side counterpart to vendor case studies for the largest SI bank; announces digital-channel awards, go-lives and partner names (e.g. NLB Klik). Cross-referencing NLB releases against Temenos/Backbase marketing is the fastest way to date and validate a vendor claim.

source_name: Slovenian business/tech press coverage of bank core-system migrations (Forbes Slovenija, Necenzurirano, Žurnal24)
why_relevant: Slovene-language reporting on the BKS Bank core-banking/payments platform migration and its post-go-live failures. Migration incidents are a reliable 'reveals-indirectly' channel: they surface the existence, timing and often the supplier of a core replacement that no vendor advertises when it goes badly.

source_name: Slovenian academic repositories (RUL / ReVIS / CEK-EF UL theses on bank IT renewal)
why_relevant: Slovene master's/diploma theses on bank information-system renewal and payment innovation frequently name the institution, the supplier and the project timeline in detail no press release provides. Slow-moving but unusually specific, and open access.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — corporate site (payments processor for Slovenian banking sector)
why_relevant: Bankart is the central Slovenian card/payments processor, founded 1997 by the majority of SI banks; it runs card issuing/acquiring processing, ATM and POS network management, the payment gateway, PSD2/open banking services, and operates the national SEPA and instant-payment systems. Its site is the single densest public trace of who owns and supplies SI payments infrastructure.

source_name: Bankart — 'Opis plačilnih sistemov za procesiranje SEPA transakcij' PDF series (SIMP-PS / BIPS scheme descriptions)
why_relevant: Authoritative, versioned scheme documentation for the SIMP-PS (SEPA) and BIPS (Bankart Instant Payment System) systems, including ISO 20022 message rules, participants and Bank of Slovenia authorisation. Re-issued periodically, so successive versions reveal infrastructure and participant change over time.

source_name: Bankart — Flik product pages and merchant onboarding documentation
why_relevant: Flik is the Slovenian instant-payment/mobile scheme built on Bankart's instant rails. Product pages plus the merchant onboarding PDFs (payment gateway, Flik e-commerce, Flik POS) expose the technical integration stack, alias/QR/NFC capability and the acquirer-merchant chain — a rare public description of a national scheme's implementation detail.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Upravljavci plačilnih sistemov (payment system operators)
why_relevant: Regulator's list of authorised payment system operators — the definitive statement of which entities legally run SI payment infrastructure (e.g. Bankart for SIMP-PS/BIPS). Ownership and authorisation changes here are leading indicators of infrastructure change.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Register subjektov nadzora (supervised entities: payment institutions, EMIs, PISP/AISP)
why_relevant: Enumerates payment institutions, e-money institutions and account information/payment initiation providers licensed in SI — the entry list for non-bank payments players (e.g. Paywiser) that buy or build issuing/processing stacks.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Poročanje upravljavcev plačilnih sistemov / poročilo o delovanju plačilnega sistema
why_relevant: Reporting instructions and templates for payment system operators reveal what infrastructure metrics exist (availability, incidents, volumes) and where derived statistics on SI payment systems can be obtained — useful for sizing and reliability comparisons between infrastructures.

source_name: FinTech Futures — Bankart/Nets Slovenian payments central infrastructure story
why_relevant: Documents the vendor selection behind Slovenia's central SCT / SCT Inst infrastructure (Nets as technology supplier to Bankart). This is exactly the kind of go-live/vendor-award trace the cell targets, and FinTech Futures covers such awards across CEE consistently.
